title: Multiple endocrine neoplasia and hereditary endocrine tumours

steps.tx: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (**MEN1**) is an autosomal dominant tumour syndrome caused by inactivating germline mutations in the **menin** tumour suppressor gene located on chromosome 11q13. The syndrome is clinically defined by tumours of the 3 Ps: **parathyroid** glands (hyperplasia or adenomas developing in over 90% of carriers by age 50), anterior pituitary adenomas (prolactinomas), and enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, predominantly duodenal **gastrinoma** causing severe peptic ulceration.
steps.say: MEN1 is an autosomal dominant syndrome caused by germline mutations in the menin tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 11q. Over ninety percent of patients develop primary hyperparathyroidism from multiglandular parathyroid tumours, alongside anterior pituitary adenomas and enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, classically duodenal gastrinomas.

vis.caption: Anatomical distribution of parathyroid, enteropancreatic, and pituitary neoplasms in MEN1. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 is driven by heterozygous gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in **RET** on chromosome 10q11. **MEN2A** features **medullary thyroid carcinoma** (developing in nearly 100% of carriers), bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma (50%), and primary hyperparathyroidism (20% to 30%). In contrast, **MEN2B** combines highly aggressive medullary thyroid carcinoma and **pheochromocytoma** with mucosal neuromas of the tongue and lips, intestinal ganglioneuromatosis, and a marfanoid habitus, lacking hyperparathyroidism.
steps.say: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 is caused by activating germline mutations in the RET proto-oncogene. MEN2A presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and hyperparathyroidism. MEN2B presents with aggressive early medullary thyroid cancer, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, and a marfanoid habitus, without parathyroid disease.

vis.caption: Comparison of neoplastic patterns between MEN2A and MEN2B RET mutations. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: In families carrying pathogenic RET mutations, the timing of **prophylactic thyroidectomy** is determined by American Thyroid Association codon risk stratification. Carriers of the highest-risk codon mutation, **M918T**, causing MEN2B, must undergo total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection within the first year of life, often within the first months. Before performing neck surgery in any MEN2 patient, clinicians must biochemically exclude or resect co-existing **pheochromocytoma** to avert fatal intraoperative hypertensive crisis.
steps.say: Prophylactic thyroidectomy in MEN2 is guided by codon-specific risk stratification. In MEN2B harboring the highest-risk M918T codon mutation, total thyroidectomy should be performed in early infancy. Pheochromocytoma must always be ruled out and resected before thyroid surgery to avoid intraoperative adrenergic crisis.

Childhood to early adulthood based on calcitonin

steps.tx: The rare syndrome **MEN4** is caused by heterozygous germline inactivating mutations in **CDKN1B**, which encodes the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p27kip1. Phenotypically, MEN4 closely mirrors classic MEN1, presenting with parathyroid adenomas, anterior pituitary tumours, and neuroendocrine neoplasms. Clinicians should pursue CDKN1B testing in patients who fulfill clinical criteria for MEN1 but test negative for mutations in the **menin** gene.
steps.say: MEN4 is caused by inactivating mutations in CDKN1B, which encodes the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p27. MEN4 closely imitates the MEN1 clinical phenotype with parathyroid and pituitary tumours, and should be investigated when genetic sequencing for menin mutations is negative.

points: Inactivating mutation in menin gene on 11q13
High penetrance of parathyroid disease (>90% by age 50)

steps.tx: The autosomal dominant hereditary cancer predisposition **von Hippel-Lindau** (**VHL**) disease is caused by germline mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25. VHL is characterized by retinal and central nervous system **hemangioblastoma**, multicentric bilateral **clear-cell renal carcinoma**, pheochromocytomas, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, and endolymphatic sac tumours. VHL-related pheochromocytomas produce predominantly norepinephrine, reflecting absent phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase.
steps.say: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is caused by mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 3p. It predisposes to retinal and central nervous system hemangioblastomas, clear-cell renal carcinomas, pheochromocytomas, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, typically producing a purely noradrenergic biochemical profile.

steps.tx: The rare autosomal dominant syndrome **Carney complex** is most frequently caused by inactivating mutations in **PRKAR1A**, which encodes the regulatory subunit type 1A of protein kinase A. Carney complex is clinically characterized by spotty facial cutaneous pigmentation (lentigines and blue nevi), **cardiac myxoma**, primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (PPNAD) causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome, testicular large cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumours, and pituitary GH-producing somatotroph adenomas.
steps.say: Carney complex is driven by inactivating mutations in PRKAR1A, leading to constitutive protein kinase A activation. Clinical features include spotty cutaneous pigmentation, cardiac myxomas, ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome from pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease, and somatotroph pituitary adenomas.

points: Paradoxical increase in cortisol during Liddle test

steps.tx: The hereditary syndrome **hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome** is caused by inactivating germline mutations in **CDC73** (formerly HRPT2), which encodes the tumour suppressor parafibromin. The syndrome is characterized by ossifying fibromas of the mandible or maxilla, renal cysts, and primary hyperparathyroidism with an exceptionally high risk of **parathyroid carcinoma** approaching 15% to 20%, mandating aggressive en bloc surgical resection rather than simple adenomectomy.
steps.say: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumour syndrome is caused by CDC73 mutations encoding the tumour suppressor parafibromin. Patients develop fibro-osseous jaw tumours, renal cysts, and severe hyperparathyroidism with a high risk of parathyroid carcinoma approaching fifteen to twenty percent.

rows: En bloc resection with ipsilateral thyroidectomy

steps.tx: Whenever **medullary thyroid carcinoma** is newly diagnosed, comprehensive germline **genetic testing** for **RET** proto-oncogene mutations must be performed prior to thyroidectomy, regardless of patient age or absent family history. Demonstrating a germline RET mutation establishes hereditary MEN2, mandating preoperative screening for pheochromocytoma, informing surgical neck dissection extent, and enabling cascade predictive genetic testing across all first-degree at-risk family members.
steps.say: All patients diagnosed with medullary thyroid carcinoma must undergo germline RET genetic testing prior to surgery. Identifying a germline RET mutation establishes hereditary MEN2, mandates urgent screening for coexisting pheochromocytoma, and directs cascade genetic testing for family members.
